title: Psalms Chapter 147 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 147 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 147 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 147.

questions.question: In Psalms 147, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: He healeth the broken in heart
The LORD lifteth up the meek
Sing unto the LORD with thanksgiving
questions.explanation: The very first statement in the chapter is 'Praise ye the LORD' which is found in Psalms 147:1.

questions.question: What does the LORD do to Jerusalem according to Psalms 147?
options: He gathereth together the outcasts of Israel
He healeth the broken in heart
He casteth the wicked down to the ground
He telleth the number of the stars
questions.correctAnswer: He gathereth together the outcasts of Israel
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'The LORD doth build up Jerusalem: he gathereth together the outcasts of Israel.' (Psalms 147:2)

questions.question: Who does the LORD heal according to Psalms 147?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states 'He healeth the broken in heart' found in Psalms 147:3.

questions.question: What does the LORD do to the wicked according to Psalms 147?
options: He casteth them down to the ground
He calleth them by their names
questions.correctAnswer: He casteth them down to the ground
questions.explanation: The text states that 'he casteth the wicked down to the ground.' (Psalms 147:6)

questions.question: How does Psalms 147 describe the LORD's understanding?
questions.explanation: The verse describes the LORD's understanding as 'his understanding is infinite.' (Psalms 147:5)

questions.question: What does Psalms 147 encourage us to do with thanksgiving?
questions.explanation: The chapter encourages to 'Sing unto the LORD with thanksgiving.' (Psalms 147:7)

questions.question: What does the LORD do for the meek according to Psalms 147?
options: He telleth the number of the stars
questions.explanation: The verse states 'The LORD lifteth up the meek.' (Psalms 147:6)

questions.question: According to Psalms 147, what is good to do?
options: To sing praises unto our God
questions.correctAnswer: To sing praises unto our God
questions.explanation: The verse states 'for it is good to sing praises unto our God.' (Psalms 147:1)

questions.question: What is said about the stars in Psalms 147?
options: He calleth them all by their names
questions.correctAnswer: He calleth them all by their names
questions.explanation: The text states 'he calleth them all by their names.' (Psalms 147:4)

questions.question: What is the tone of the singing encouraged in Psalms 147?
questions.explanation: The verse encourages joyful singing 'Sing unto the LORD with thanksgiving.' (Psalms 147:7)

questions.question: What does the LORD do to the broken according to Psalms 147?
questions.explanation: The verse states 'and bindeth up their wounds.' (Psalms 147:3)

questions.question: True or False: The LORD builds up Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: The verse states 'The LORD doth build up Jerusalem.' (Psalms 147:2)

questions.question: True or False: The LORD's understanding is finite.
questions.explanation: The verse states 'his understanding is infinite.' (Psalms 147:5), therefore, the statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD heals the strong.
questions.explanation: The text states that 'He healeth the broken in heart.' (Psalms 147:3), not the strong.

questions.question: True or False: Singing praises unto God is described as pleasant.
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'for it is pleasant; and praise is comely.' (Psalms 147:1), which means it is indeed pleasant.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 147 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 147 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does God prepare for the earth according to Psalms 147:8?
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:8 states that God covers the heaven with clouds, prepares rain for the earth, and makes grass to grow upon the mountains.

questions.question: What does Psalms 147:11 promise will happen if someone fears the Lord?
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:11 indicates that the Lord takes pleasure in those who fear Him and hope in His mercy.

questions.question: According to Psalms 147:10, what does God not take pleasure in?
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:10 explicitly states that God does not delight in the strength of the horse or the legs of a man.

questions.question: What connection is made between fearing the Lord and hope in His mercy in Psalms 147:11?
options: Both are pleasing to the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: Both are pleasing to the Lord
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:11 shows that the Lord takes pleasure in those who fear Him and hope in His mercy, connecting both attributes.

questions.question: What does Psalms 147:13 say God has strengthened?
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:13 mentions that God has strengthened the bars of Jerusalem's gates.

questions.question: According to Psalms 147:14, what does God fill His people with?
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:14 states that God fills His people with the finest of the wheat, indicating His provision.

questions.question: What is the nature of God's understanding as described in Psalms 147:5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:5 describes God's understanding as infinite, emphasizing His omniscience.

questions.question: How does Psalms 147:3 describe God's action towards the brokenhearted?
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:3 states that God healeth the broken in heart and bindeth up their wounds.

questions.question: What does Psalms 147:2 highlight about God's relationship with Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:2 emphasizes that the Lord builds up Jerusalem and gathers together the outcasts of Israel.

questions.question: According to Psalms 147:6, what does God do to the meek?
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:6 states that the Lord lifteth up the meek, indicating His care for the humble.

questions.question: What does Psalms 147:1 encourage people to do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:1 encourages people to praise the Lord, affirming that it is good and pleasant.

questions.question: What does Psalms 147:7 instruct believers to do with thanksgiving?
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:7 instructs believers to sing unto the Lord with thanksgiving, highlighting the importance of gratitude in worship.

questions.question: The Lord takes pleasure in those who fear Him according to Psalms 147:11.
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:11 clearly states that the Lord takes pleasure in them that fear Him.

questions.question: God has no concern for the needs of the beasts according to Psalms 147:9.
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:9 indicates that God gives food to the beasts and to young ravens which cry, showing His concern for all creation.

questions.question: God delights in the strength of man according to Psalms 147:10.
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:10 states that God does not take pleasure in the legs of a man, indicating that His delight lies elsewhere.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 147 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 147.

questions.question: What does the Lord send forth upon the earth according to Psalms 147:15?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'He sendeth forth his commandment upon earth...' indicating that it is His commandment that is sent.

questions.question: According to Psalms 147:16, how does the Lord give snow?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions, 'He giveth snow like wool...' showing the softness and purity associated with snow.

questions.question: What does Psalms 147:17 compare the casting of ice to?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'He casteth forth his ice like morsels...' which implies that ice is dispensed in small portions.

questions.question: What happens when the Lord sends out His word in Psalms 147:18?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'He sendeth out his word, and melteth them...' indicating the power of His word to change conditions.

questions.question: To whom does the Lord show His word according to Psalms 147:19?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates, 'He sheweth his word unto Jacob...' signifying a special relationship with Jacob and Israel.

questions.question: What has the Lord not done with any other nation according to Psalms 147:20?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'He hath not dealt so with any nation...' highlighting the unique relationship with Israel.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'דָּבָר' (dabar) in Psalms 147:15 mean?
questions.explanation: In Hebrew, 'דָּבָר' translates as 'word', which is used in Psalms 147:15 to denote the command of God.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Psalms 147:16's description of snow?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'He giveth snow like wool' employs a simile by comparing snow to wool using 'like'.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of God's provision as seen in Psalms 147:9?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:26 echoes the theme of God's provision, stating that He feeds the birds of the air, similar to Psalms 147:9.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the theme of God's healing in Psalms 147:3?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 53:5 speaks of healing through Christ, fulfilling the theme of healing found in Psalms 147:3.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Psalms 147:15?
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:14 precedes 15, discussing God's provision and peace before His commandment is sent.

questions.question: How does Psalms 147:4 reflect God's omniscience?
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:4 highlights God's omniscience, stating, 'He telleth the number of the stars; he calleth them all by their names.'

questions.question: Psalms 147:11 indicates that the Lord takes pleasure in which group?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'The LORD taketh pleasure in them that fear him, in those that hope in his mercy,' specifically mentioning the meek.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 147:20 states that God has dealt with all nations in the same way as Israel.
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:20 states, 'He hath not dealt so with any nation,' indicating a unique relationship with Israel.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 147:3 affirms that the Lord heals the brokenhearted.
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:3 states, 'He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds,' affirming His healing power.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 147 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 147 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 147:3 teach about God's nature in relation to human suffering?
options: God is indifferent to human pain
God actively heals and comforts the brokenhearted
questions.correctAnswer: God actively heals and comforts the brokenhearted
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:3 states that God "healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds," teaching that God is compassionate and restorative toward those who suffer.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's providence is taught in Psalms 147:4?
options: God limits His knowledge to only earthly affairs
God knows and names every star, showing His infinite knowledge and control over creation
God created the stars but has no ongoing relationship with them
God delegates the care of the universe to angels
questions.correctAnswer: God knows and names every star, showing His infinite knowledge and control over creation
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:4 says God "telleth the number of the stars; he calleth them all by their names," illustrating God's omniscience and sovereign control over creation.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning God's justice and mercy is taught in Psalms 147:6?
options: God is neutral toward the meek and the wicked
God exalts the meek and humbles the wicked, demonstrating His just governance
God only judges the wicked but ignores the meek
God shows mercy only to the powerful
questions.correctAnswer: God exalts the meek and humbles the wicked, demonstrating His just governance
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:6 states, "The LORD lifteth up the meek: he casteth the wicked down to the ground," showing both God's justice in judging the wicked and His mercy in uplifting the humble.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 147:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:5 says "Great is our Lord, and of great power: his understanding is infinite," highlighting God's omniscience—His infinite understanding.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Psalms 147:15?
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:15 states, "He sendeth forth his commandment upon earth: his word runneth very swiftly," demonstrating God's sovereign authority over creation.

questions.question: How does Psalms 147:12–14 connect to the theme of God's covenant promises elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It denies God's faithfulness to Israel
It reaffirms God's covenant blessings of peace, protection, and provision for Jerusalem
It introduces a new covenant unrelated to the Old Testament
It emphasizes God's judgment without mercy
questions.correctAnswer: It reaffirms God's covenant blessings of peace, protection, and provision for Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Verses 12–14 praise God for strengthening Jerusalem's gates, blessing her children, making peace in her borders, and filling her with wheat, echoing covenant promises of protection and provision (cf. Deuteronomy 28).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection can be drawn from Psalms 147:19–20 regarding God's revelation to Israel?
options: God revealed His laws equally to all nations
God uniquely revealed His statutes and judgments to Israel as His chosen people
God rejected Israel and gave revelation only to the Gentiles
God's word was unknown to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God uniquely revealed His statutes and judgments to Israel as His chosen people
questions.explanation: Verses 19–20 highlight that God showed His word, statutes, and judgments specifically to Israel, and not to other nations, underscoring the special covenant relationship with Israel.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 147:10 and Psalms 147:11 teach about the basis of God's pleasure?
options: God delights in human strength and physical abilities
God takes pleasure only in the wealth of nations
God delights in those who fear Him and hope in His mercy rather than worldly power
God is indifferent to human attitudes
questions.correctAnswer: God delights in those who fear Him and hope in His mercy rather than worldly power
questions.explanation: Verse 10 denies God's delight in horses or human strength, while verse 11 affirms that He takes pleasure in those who fear Him and hope in His mercy, teaching that spiritual reverence and trust are what please God.

questions.question: What doctrinal synthesis about God's providence and natural order is taught by Psalms 147:8 and Psalms 147:9?
options: God is uninvolved in nature's provision
God sustains creation by providing rain, grass, and food to animals, demonstrating providential care
God only cares for humans, not animals
questions.correctAnswer: God sustains creation by providing rain, grass, and food to animals, demonstrating providential care
questions.explanation: Verse 8 describes God covering the heavens with clouds and preparing rain for the earth, while verse 9 notes God giving food to beasts and young ravens, together teaching God's providential sustenance of all creation.

questions.question: What synthesis of doctrine about God's power and control over nature is taught in Psalms 147:16 and Psalms 147:18?
options: God has no influence over weather phenomena
God controls natural elements such as snow, frost, ice, and wind, demonstrating His sovereign power over creation
Natural forces exist apart from God
God only controls the sun and moon
questions.correctAnswer: God controls natural elements such as snow, frost, ice, and wind, demonstrating His sovereign power over creation
questions.explanation: Verse 16 speaks of God giving snow and scattering frost, and verse 18 describes God sending His word to melt ice and causing wind to blow, showing His sovereign command over natural elements.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that Psalms 147:19-20 shows God is partial and unjust by revealing His laws only to Israel. What does the passage actually teach?
options: God's revelation to Israel is a unique covenantal relationship, not injustice or partiality
God is unjust because He withholds His laws from other nations
God has no interest in justice
God revealed His laws equally but Israel ignored them
questions.correctAnswer: God's revelation to Israel is a unique covenantal relationship, not injustice or partiality
questions.explanation: The passage (Psalms 147:19-20) emphasizes that God uniquely revealed His statutes to Israel, highlighting the special covenant relationship rather than injustice or unfairness.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 147:2 teach about God's work of restoration and salvation?
options: God abandons those who are outcast
God gathers together the outcasts of Israel, signifying His redemptive restoration
God restores only the righteous, ignoring the broken
questions.correctAnswer: God gathers together the outcasts of Israel, signifying His redemptive restoration
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:2 states God "doth build up Jerusalem: he gathereth together the outcasts of Israel," teaching God's restorative work in salvation history.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is chiefly illustrated in Psalms 147:1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 147:1 calls on praise because "it is good to sing praises unto our God; for it is pleasant; and praise is comely," emphasizing God's goodness as the basis for worship.

questions.question: How does Psalms 147:13 teach about God's covenant faithfulness to His people?
options: God ignores the security of His people
God strengthens and blesses Jerusalem, indicating His protective covenant faithfulness
God only blesses individuals, not communities
God weakens the gates of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: God strengthens and blesses Jerusalem, indicating His protective covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Verse 13 says, "For he hath strengthened the bars of thy gates; he hath blessed thy children within thee," showing God's active covenant care and protection.

questions.question: What theological insight about God's communicative action is taught by Psalms 147:18 and Psalms 147:15?
options: God's word is powerless and slow
God's word is powerful and swift, able to command natural phenomena and accomplish His purposes
God only communicates through human prophets
God's word is limited to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God's word is powerful and swift, able to command natural phenomena and accomplish His purposes
questions.explanation: Verse 15 says God's word "runneth very swiftly" and verse 18 shows that God "sendeth out his word, and melteth" ice and causes wind, teaching the power and efficacy of God's word.
